title: Quarterly Commitment Conductor: orchestration for Hosted API + Model Catalog runway
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: produce a compact, executable quarterly plan (commitment conductor) that maps feature deliverables, model rotations, canary windows, and contingency lanes for the Hosted API + Model Catalog surface. This ticket coordinates cross-functional tradeoffs between cost, latency SLOs, and model quality guardrails so engineering, design, and PMs have a single source of truth for execution and escalation during the quarter. Scope includes: release lane definitions, canary/fallback policy defaults, model onboarding cadence, runway capacity buffers for Dedicated, and a set of validated prompt+eval checklists for regression monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: A single quarterly commitment matrix published to Confluence that lists deliverable -> owner -> canary window -> rollback criteria
Model rotation lanes defined (stable, preview, canary) with explicit fallback mappings and latency/cost thresholds
Approved canary scheduling template and automated calendar invites for infra + SRE runbooks
Eval suites (prompt sets) attached for top 10 hosted endpoints with baseline metrics and regression alerts configured in the Console
Dependencies enumerated and at-risk items flagged with mitigation plans
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with Eng (runtime, infra), Design, and SRE. Agreed to prioritize 3 high-risk endpoints for controlled model rotation this quarter. Action: ENG to produce capacity profile by 2026-03-08.
2026-03-05: Draft commitment matrix created (Confluence). Added preliminary canary windows—feedback from SRE: prefer shorter canaries for low-traffic endpoints. Updated matrix accordingly.

2026-03-07: Product design review. Design requested clearer UX signaling for active canaries in Console and a low-noise notification flow for customer-impacting rollouts. Follow-up ticket recommended (DES-4029).

2026-03-08: ENG capacity profile received (ENG-1842 referenced). Key trade-off: to keep latency SLOs for endpoint X we either reserve Dedicated slots (higher cost) or accept 5-10% higher p95 during peak. PM recommended canary-first approach plus dynamic routing to cheaper quantized variants for background traffic.

2026-03-09: Security review triage: model onboarding checklist requires KMS policy audit for any private deployments. Security review flagged for targeted endpoints; created dependency PM-991240 for coordination with Security team.

2026-03-10: Matrix ready for stakeholder review. Uploaded plan and link to evaluation dashboards; scheduled 2026-03-12 decision review with GTM and Solutions Engineering. Noted follow-ups: finalize rollback criteria language and wire up Console alerting thresholds.
notes: Decision logs: prefer staged canaries with automated rollback on quality-regression or p95 breach > 30% above baseline

Trade-offs considered: reserved Dedicated capacity vs. dynamic routing to quantized models for cost control; elected to layer both options (reserved for top 3 endpoints, routing for background workloads)
Ops playbook stub: one-pager linked from Confluence; includes escalation matrix, contact list, and rollback commands
Follow-ups: create a small automation task to tag canary requests in traces for easier sampling (ENG spike planned).
